expected: Applicants (architects, builders and private homeowners) can submit a building permit application with all required documents online.
explanation: Online submission of the application with all documents is captured, and homeowners are included via usability testing.

expected: The system checks completeness before submission and prevents submitting without required documents such as the neighbour consent or signature.
explanation: Submission is blocked when required documents such as the neighbour consent are missing, and signature handling is raised as an open question.

expected: Applicants can upload large plan PDFs (files of around 200 MB are common).
explanation: Uploads of PDF plans of up to 200 MB are specified.

expected: Applicants can see the status of their application online (received, in review, additional documents needed, decision made).
explanation: Online status view with the four named statuses is specified.

expected: Internal comments, such as concerns from the fire protection office, are not visible to applicants.
explanation: Internal comments and statements, including fire protection concerns, are hidden from applicants.

expected: External offices such as fire protection can review dossiers and submit their statements in the system.
explanation: Offices such as fire protection are assigned dossiers and submit statements in the system.

expected: Login with roles, including access for external authorities.
explanation: Personal role-based logins are specified, including restricted roles for external authorities.

expected: Every access to and change of a dossier is logged, so it can be shown in an appeal who saw and changed what.
explanation: Every access and change is logged tamper-proof and can be viewed and exported for appeals.

expected: Data is stored in Switzerland (requirement of the cantonal data protection office).
explanation: Storage and processing exclusively in Swiss data centres is required.

expected: The portal is available in German and English.
explanation: The full UI is available in German and English.

expected: The portal meets the federal accessibility standard and works with screen readers.
explanation: The federal accessibility standard and screen reader operability are required.

expected: The decision can be delivered electronically, but only if the applicant has agreed to electronic delivery.
explanation: Electronic delivery of rulings is allowed only with recorded consent.

expected: Applicants who are not comfortable with computers are supported, e.g. counter staff digitise a paper application.
explanation: Counter staff digitise paper applications, and less experienced users are included in usability testing.

expected: Retention rules: building files are kept for the life of the building; other documents such as correspondence for a period still to be confirmed (around 10 years).
explanation: Building files are kept for the building's lifetime, and other documents follow a period to be confirmed (assumed ten years).

expected: Will paper submissions still be accepted, and if so who digitises them? (Disagreement between the Head of Building Department and the Permit Clerk; council decision needed.)
explanation: The paper-channel conflict between Rossi and Keller is raised for a council decision.

expected: What upload performance is acceptable? "Fast" was not quantified.
explanation: The unquantified upload time target is raised as an open question.

expected: First release by next summer covers online submission and status tracking; integration with the canton comes later.
explanation: The first release by next summer covers submission and status tracking, with canton integration deferred.

expected: Success: most applications arrive online, fewer completeness letters (target: half) and fewer status phone calls.
explanation: Halving completeness letters and reducing status calls are captured, but the goal that most applications arrive online is only tracked, not stated as a target.
